about: Roles shown on the GEO board, by NORAD catalogue number. An object is listed only where published reporting supports the role; each entry cites it. Unlisted objects have no listed role, which says nothing about what they are. Curated by hand; checked 26 Oct 2026, widened from Secure World Foundation's RPO sheet 27 Nov 2026 (docs/validation/geo-board.md).

roles.inspection: Inspection-capable: publicly reported rendezvous, proximity operations or inspection of other satellites
roles.servicing: Servicing: docks with client satellites (life extension or refuelling)

objects.name: LUCH-5X (OLYMP-K 2)
objects.basis: Moved along the belt after its March 2023 launch, stopping near commercial satellites; closest measured about 16 km (Slingshot Aerospace)

objects.name: USA 270 (GSSAP 3)
objects.basis: US Space Force GSSAP satellite: operates near GEO and manoeuvres to inspect objects in the belt

objects.name: USA 271 (GSSAP 4)
objects.basis: US Space Force GSSAP satellite: operates near GEO and manoeuvres to inspect objects in the belt

objects.name: USA 324 (GSSAP 5)
objects.basis: US Space Force GSSAP satellite (launched Jan 2022): operates near GEO and manoeuvres to inspect objects in the belt

objects.name: USA 325 (GSSAP 6)
objects.basis: US Space Force GSSAP satellite (launched Jan 2022): operates near GEO and manoeuvres to inspect objects in the belt

objects.name: SHIJIAN-17 (SJ-17)
objects.basis: Chinese experimental satellite; circumnavigated ChinaSat-5A and later approached ChinaSat-6B and Shijian-20

objects.name: SHIJIAN-21 (SJ-21)
objects.basis: Docked with the defunct BeiDou-2 G2 and towed it about 3,000 km above GEO in January 2022; reported docked with Shijian-25 in 2025

objects.name: SHIJIAN-25 (SJ-25)
objects.basis: Built to test refuelling and life extension; tracking firms reported it docked with Shijian-21 in mid-2025 (not confirmed by China)

objects.name: MEV-1
objects.basis: Northrop Grumman Mission Extension Vehicle: docks with client satellites to extend their life

objects.name: MEV-2
objects.basis: Northrop Grumman Mission Extension Vehicle; docked to Intelsat 10-02 on 12 Apr 2021, undocking planned for 2026

objects.name: USA 253 (GSSAP 1)
objects.basis: US Space Force GSSAP satellite (launched Jul 2014): operates near GEO and manoeuvres to inspect objects in the belt
sources: Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: USA 254 (GSSAP 2)
objects.basis: US Space Force GSSAP satellite (launched Jul 2014): operates near GEO and manoeuvres to inspect objects in the belt
sources: Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: USA 255 (ANGELS)
objects.basis: AFRL experiment launched with GSSAP 1 and 2 in Jul 2014: manoeuvred around its own Delta IV upper stage above GEO, from about 50 km to within a few km; decommissioned Nov 2017
sources: Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: LUCH (OLYMP-K 1)
objects.basis: Russian satellite (launched Sep 2014): parked between Intelsat 901 and Intelsat 7 in 2015, later beside Intelsat 905; France's armed forces minister said it approached Athena-Fidus in 2017. Reported moved to a graveyard orbit in Oct 2025 and partly broken up in Jan 2026
sources: Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: TJS-3
objects.basis: Chinese satellite (launched Dec 2018): manoeuvred in step with a companion first catalogued as its apogee kick motor, then left its slot in May 2019 as the companion took its place; COMSPOC read this as practice at confusing other nations' tracking
sources: Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: TJS-3 AKM (TJS-3's companion)
objects.basis: Catalogued as TJS-3's apogee kick motor, but kept station and manoeuvred in step with TJS-3 from Jan 2019 and took its place in May 2019; China has not acknowledged a second object
sources: Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: SHIYAN 12 01 (SY-12 01)
objects.basis: Chinese test satellite (launched Dec 2021): when a GSSAP satellite (USA 270) approached in early 2022, the pair moved off in opposite directions and SY-12 02 took up a position to view it (COMSPOC, reported by SpaceNews)
sources: SpaceNews: An in-orbit game of cat and mouse
Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: SHIYAN 12 02 (SY-12 02)
objects.basis: Chinese test satellite (launched Dec 2021): when a GSSAP satellite (USA 270) approached in early 2022, the pair moved off in opposite directions and SY-12 02 moved to a sunlit view of it (COMSPOC, reported by SpaceNews)
sources: SpaceNews: An in-orbit game of cat and mouse
Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: LINUSS2
objects.basis: Lockheed Martin CubeSat (launched Nov 2022 on USSF-44): rendezvous and proximity operations with LINUSS1 above GEO in early 2023, to within about 400 m, as a servicing demonstration
sources: Aviation Week: LINUSS rendezvous within 400 m
Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)

objects.name: LDPE-3A
objects.basis: US Space Force propulsive ESPA vehicle (launched Jan 2023 on USSF-67): Secure World Foundation lists proximity operations with Shijian-23 in Oct 2024 (the only published report found)
sources: Secure World Foundation, RPO data of the Global Counterspace Capabilities report (sheet updated 17 Feb 2026)
